title: The Attic Letters
text:
My grandmother kept her letters in a biscuit tin beneath the attic stairs, and I discovered them only after her funeral. The envelopes were brittle at the edges, and many had been opened so often that the creases had softened into fabric. Reading them, I felt less like an heir than a trespasser, eavesdropping on a conversation that had ended decades before I was born.

What struck me most was not the grief they described but the stubborn cheerfulness that ran through them. She wrote about a failed harvest with the same wit she reserved for her rivals at church. Only in the final letter did the mask slip, and even then she apologised for troubling me with her fears.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, where did the narrator find the letters?
options: In a biscuit tin beneath the attic stairs
In a desk drawer in the study
Inside a trunk at the church
In a box sent by post

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what did the grandmother write about with wit?
What does the narrator imply when he says he felt like a trespasser?
options: He felt he had lost the letters through carelessness
He felt tired after a long journey
He felt the letters had been forged
He felt he had no right to read such private writing

questions.text: What can be inferred about the grandmother's cheerful tone in her letters?
options: She wrote cheerfully only to impress her rivals at church
She had recovered from an illness by the time she wrote them
She was indifferent to the harvest failures
It concealed fears that she rarely expressed openly

vocabulary.definition: hard but easily broken or cracked
a person who enters or intrudes where they have no right to be
secretly listening to a private conversation
refusing to change one's attitude or behaviour despite pressure

paragraph_translations: Моя бабуся зберігала листи в бляшаній коробці під сходами на горищі, і я знайшов їх лише після її похорону. Конверти були крихкими по краях, а багато з них так часто відкривали, що згини стали м'якими, мов тканина. Читаючи їх, я відчував себе радше непроханим гостем, ніж спадкоємцем, ніби підслуховував розмову, що закінчилася за десятки років до мого народження.

Найбільше мене вразила не скорбота, про яку вони розповідали, а впертий жартівливий настрій, що проходив крізь них. Вона писала про невдалий урожай з тією ж дотепністю, яку берегла для суперниць у церкві. Лише в останньому листі маска спала, і навіть тоді вона вибачалася, що турбує мене своїми страхами.
